title: Acts of Compassion
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 8 Christian Religious Education; not yet checked by a CRE teacher; not loaded by the live tutor

skills.key_step: The learner describes the church's role in helping the needy, lists who should be helped (the elderly and foreigners, Leviticus 19:32-33; the weak, the fatherless, the poor and oppressed, Psalm 82:3), relates the acts of compassion in Matthew 25:31-40, establishes who inherits the kingdom (those who served the least) and distinguishes the unrighteous acts of Matthew 25:41-46 (failing to help).

floor.prerequisite: Knows ways of helping the needy.
floor.question: Why did Jesus feed the four thousand?

representations: two groups drawn: sheep and goats
a list of the needy from Leviticus 19 and Psalm 82

board.do: Draw two groups: sheep on the right, goats on the left.
Wait for the learner to say fed, welcomed, clothed, visited.
List the six acts and who should be helped.

misconceptions.ask: Which act does the king name in Matthew 25:35?
misconceptions.repair: Read Matthew 25:35-36 and list the six acts: food, drink, welcome, clothes, care, visiting.
Separate child safety (stay with trusted adults) from welcoming strangers in need as a family or church (Matthew 25:35).

misconceptions.ask: What does the king say about helping the least?
misconceptions.repair: Read Matthew 25:40: "you did for me". Helping the least is serving Christ.

misconceptions.ask: Who will inherit the kingdom, according to Matthew 25:34-40?
misconceptions.repair: Read Matthew 25:34-36: "come, you who are blessed... for I was hungry and you gave me something to eat".

checks.question: Name an act of compassion in Matthew 25:35-36.
checks.answer: Feeding the hungry (welcoming strangers, visiting the sick)

checks.question: Who will inherit the kingdom, according to Matthew 25:34-40?
